title: BOS-976 — a login shell that cannot answer inside the agent-probe budget now blocks startup with a timeout that names the shell and the budget, instead of claiming the agent was not found

scenes.title: A slow interactive rc lands on the probe-timed-out screen, which says the shell ran out of time rather than sending the user hunting a PATH problem

waitFor.label: the probe's deadline produces a screen that says so — before BOS-976 the same 20 seconds ended on 'claude was not found for this project' and the agent resolved perfectly well

steps.caption: The preset's login shell sources a .bashrc that sleeps well past the probe budget, so boss's real `command -v claude` probe really runs out of time. Nothing paints until it does: the wait is deliberately longer than the 20s budget so a loaded CI box cannot cut the probe short and turn a real capture into an unexplained timeout.

expect.label: the headline names the operation, the agent and the elapsed budget, so a user who waited 20 seconds gets a diagnosis rather than a dead end
the budget is on screen as a number the user can act on — it is rendered from agentResolveTimeout, so it cannot drift from the bound that actually elapsed
the login shell the probe ran is named, which is the thing the user has to go and time
the screen rules out the wrong diagnosis explicitly — this is the whole defect, so a message that merely stopped saying 'not found' would not be enough
the way out is on the SAME frame as the timeout: one regex over one screen, so the user is not stranded on a blocking screen they cannot dismiss

steps.caption: The timeout screen: the elapsed budget, the shell that was too slow, an explicit denial that the agent is missing, and a live way out. The matcher has no negative form, so the counterpart — that a genuine non-zero `command -v` still renders today's not-found screen byte for byte — is pinned as a literal in TestCheckAgentResolvableBranchesOnProbeOutcome rather than asserted here.
